finding: entry-failure-boundary-review.mjs asserts turns.status === 'failed' for the committed-but-unpreparable Enter scenarios (malformed-committed-reply, catalog-error-after-commit). The durable host turn cannot hold that value.
classification: Reviewer expectation error, not a D-Enter regression: 'failed' is not in the host's durable turn vocabulary (running | completed | aborted | error). Requesting it over the supported RPC coerces silently to 'completed' — the exact status the review rejects — while 'error' is the host's failure terminal. The product-side facts the review actually requires are green: exactly one provider request, zero tool side effects, a desktop-visible terminal error, the committed mode kept durable, and the next real prompt recovering from the durable row.

evidence.hostWriter: app/crates/host-core/src/sessions.rs:3413-3449 — end_turn_settling maps status to completed|aborted|error (anything else -> completed) and is the only writer of turns.status
evidence.fixedPiParity: upstream/pi-desktop/crates/host-core/src/sessions.rs:3237-3248 — the pinned reference has the same three-value match
evidence.probeResult: session.endTurn {status:"failed"} -> stored "completed"; {status:"error"} -> stored "error" (real host binary, isolated SQLite, direct row read)
